mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement H4M 630 engine for a Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV typically costs £2,000-£4,500 for the supply-only unit. Fitting adds 10-14 hours of labour at £65-£90/hr, bringing the total fitted cost to £3,000-£5,500 at an independent specialist. Dealer pricing is significantly higher, with some owners reporting quotes in the £5,000-£8,000 range for a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of gearbox or electric motor failure in a Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is a clunky or jerky transition between petrol and electric power, particularly at around 30mph. More serious symptoms include drivetrain noise, loss of power, warning lights, and complete transmission failure. Some owners have reported gearbox failure at mileages as low as 29,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is the Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV a reliable car?

acceptedAnswer.text: The E-Tech PHEV is relatively new, so long-term reliability data is limited. The 1.6-litre petrol engine itself is a proven unit, but the complex hybrid gearbox has been a source of complaints. Some owners report trouble-free ownership, while others have experienced significant drivetrain issues at relatively low mileages.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value. Early examples (2020-2021) are worth £11,000-£18,000 - a full engine replacement at £3,000-£5,500 may represent 20-40% of the car's value, which is often justifiable if the rest of the car is in good condition. However, if the gearbox and electric motor have also failed, total repair costs can exceed £7,000, making replacement uneconomical.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Megane E-Tech PHEV and the Megane E-Tech Electric?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Megane E-Tech PHEV (plug-in hybrid) combines a 1.6-litre petrol engine with two electric motors and a 9.8 kWh battery, offering up to 30 miles of pure-electric range. The Megane E-Tech Electric is a fully electric vehicle with a 40kWh or 60kWh battery and no combustion engine. They are completely different vehicles with different platforms and powertrains.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to charge a Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 9.8 kWh battery takes approximately three hours to charge from zero to 100% using a Type 2 charger, or just over four hours using a domestic three-pin socket. The onboard charger operates at up to 3.6kW. The battery warranty covers 8 years or 100,000 miles.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Megane E-Tech Plug-in Hybrid represents a significant step in Renault's electrification strategy, bringing Formula 1-inspired hybrid technology to the family hatchback segment. First introduced on the Sport Tourer estate in late 2020 and arriving on the hatchback in mid-2021, the E-Tech PHEV effectively replaced conventional petrol and diesel Megane variants. The powertrain combines a naturally aspirated 1.6-litre petrol engine with two electric motors and a clutchless multi-mode gearbox, delivering 160hp and offering up to 30 miles of pure-electric range.

milestones.description: Megane E-Tech PHEV first introduced on Sport Tourer estate; 1.6-litre naturally aspirated petrol engine (H4M 630) paired with two electric motors and a 9.8 kWh battery
Hatchback version launched in the UK from £29,495; available in Iconic and R.S. Line trims
present - E-Tech PHEV becomes the only non-EV powertrain option in the Megane range
Continued production with minor updates; battery warranty remains 8 years/100,000 miles

commonProblems.h2: Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV (H4M 630) is a relatively new powertrain, but several issues have already been reported by UK and European owners. The 1.6-litre petrol engine itself is generally reliable, but the hybrid system's integration with the clutchless multi-mode gearbox introduces unique failure points. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing known failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Gearbox & Electric Motor Failure - Clunky Shifts and Drivetrain Issues in the Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV
problems.rootCause: The E-Tech PHEV uses a clutchless multi-mode dog gearbox developed by Renault. Some owners report a clunky or jerky transition between petrol and electric power, with the power sources switching at around 30mph. More seriously, some owners have reported complete gearbox failure requiring replacement of one of the electric motors - with one owner reporting failure at just 29,000 miles, one month after warranty expiry.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Dealer-level software update and transmission adaptation reset
repairOptions.longevity: First-line response for clunky shifts; may resolve software-related issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the multi-mode gearbox and/or electric motor unit
repairOptions.longevity: Required if internal mechanical failure has occurred; often the only viable solution

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete H4M 630 engine + gearbox + electric motor replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable on high-value examples; often exceeds vehicle value on older models

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply this UK-wide decision framework to your Renault Megane E-Tech PHEV. Early examples (2020-2021) with average mileage typically range from £11,000-£18,000. Later, lower-mileage examples (2022-2024) range from £18,000-£28,000. - Vehicle worth under ~£14,000: used engine or gearbox repair typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit - Vehicle worth ~£14,000-£20,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years - Vehicle worth £20,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value
problems.recommendation: If your Megane E-Tech PHEV exhibits clunky shifts or jerky transitions, have the software checked first - many drivability issues can be resolved with a dealer-level update. If you experience more serious drivetrain noise or failure, a specialist inspection is essential. Gearbox and electric motor replacement is expensive, so always obtain multiple quotes before committing.

problems.h4: Charging System & Battery Issues - Charging Flap Failures and Intermittent Charging
problems.rootCause: The charging flap mechanism is a known weak point, with reports of the flap failing to open or close properly. Some owners have also reported intermittent failures to begin charging.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the charging flap locking pin or mechanism
repairOptions.longevity: Simple fix; often resolves the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full diagnostic of charging system, including onboard charger and battery management
repairOptions.longevity: Required if the vehicle intermittently fails to charge

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Repair or replacement of BMS components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if charging issues are related to battery management

problems.recommendation: If your Megane E-Tech PHEV won't charge or the charging flap is stuck, have it inspected promptly. The flap mechanism repair is relatively inexpensive, but charging system diagnostics may be more complex. The 9.8 kWh battery carries an 8-year/100,000-mile warranty, so battery-related issues may be covered if the car is still within the warranty period.
